problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate shipments onto identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Component A: mass 39 tons
* Component B: mass 44 tons
* Component C: mass 61 tons
* Component D: mass 64 tons
* Component E: mass 41 tons
* Component F: mass 33 tons
* Component G: mass 59 tons
* Component H: mass 41 tons
* Component I: mass 63 tons
* Component J: mass 60 tons
* Component K: mass 38 tons
* Component L: mass 31 tons
* Component M: mass 45 tons
* Component N: mass 41 tons
* Component O: mass 42 tons
* Component P: mass 68 tons
* Component Q: mass 32 tons
* Component R: mass 51 tons
* Component S: mass 52 tons
* Component T: mass 60 tons
* Component U: mass 49 tons
* Component V: mass 51 tons
* Component W: mass 66 tons
* Component X: mass 51 tons
* Component Y: mass 50 tons
* Component Z: mass 35 tons
* Component [: mass 49 tons
* Component \: mass 70 tons
* Component ]: mass 55 tons
* Component ^: mass 34 tons
* Component _: mass 61 tons
* Component `: mass 69 tons
* Component a: mass 70 tons
* Component b: mass 50 tons
* Component c: mass 67 tons
* Component d: mass 52 tons
* Component e: mass 57 tons
* Component f: mass 36 tons
* Component g: mass 37 tons

Each aircraft has a maximum payload capacity of 100 tons. Allocate every shipment to a plane while using the fewest possible aircraft. Each shipment must be placed on exactly one plane, and the cumulative mass on any aircraft cannot surpass its payload limit.
